Marketing Fundamentals: Marketing
The activities that create, communicate, and deliver value to customers
Marketing concept
The philosophy that satisfying customer needs drives profit
Need versus want
A basic requirement versus a specific way of satisfying it
Target market
The specific group of customers a business aims to serve
Value proposition
The clear statement of the benefit a customer receives
Utility
The usefulness a product provides, in form, place, time, or possession
Marketing mix
The controllable variables of product, price, place, and promotion
Marketing environment
The external forces shaping marketing decisions
Customer relationship management
Systems and practices for building long-term customer loyalty
Business-to-consumer marketing
Selling directly to individual end users
Business-to-business marketing
Selling to organisations rather than individuals
Nonprofit marketing
Applying marketing techniques to promote causes rather than profit
The Marketing Mix: Product element
The good, service, or idea offered to satisfy a need
Price element
What the customer gives up in exchange for the product
Place element
How and where the product reaches the customer
Promotion element
The communication used to inform and persuade buyers
Four Ps
The shorthand name for product, price, place, and promotion
Product mix
The full set of products a company offers
Product line
A group of closely related products within the mix
Service marketing extension
Adding people, process, and physical evidence for services
Intangibility of services
Services cannot be seen or touched before purchase
Marketing strategy
The plan for selecting a target market and building a mix for it
Integrated marketing
Coordinating every mix element to send one consistent message
Trade-offs in the mix
Changing one element usually forces adjustment in the others
Market Research: The systematic gathering of information about customers and markets
Information collected firsthand for the current project
Information already collected for another purpose
Research producing descriptive insight rather than numbers
Research producing numerical, statistically analysable data
A guided discussion with a small group of target customers
Recording customer behaviour without direct questioning
The subset of a population actually studied
Error introduced when a sample does not represent the population
A question worded to push respondents toward one answer
Launching in a limited area to evaluate response before full release
Turning collected information into usable marketing conclusions
Consumer Behavior: The study of how people decide what to buy
Recognition, search, evaluation, purchase, and post-purchase steps
The stage where a customer notices an unmet need
The stage where a customer gathers options
Judging whether the product met expectations
Buyer doubt or regret following a significant purchase
A buying reason based on logic, such as price or durability
A buying reason based on feeling, such as status or comfort
An unplanned buying decision made at point of sale
How peers and admired groups shape buying choices
A customer's consistent preference for one brand
Appealing to needs from basic survival to self-fulfilment
Market Segmentation and Targeting: Market segmentation
Dividing a broad market into smaller similar groups
Demographic segmentation
Grouping by age, income, education, or family status
Geographic segmentation
Grouping by location, climate, or region
Psychographic segmentation
Grouping by lifestyle, values, and personality
Behavioral segmentation
Grouping by usage rate, loyalty, or benefits sought
Mass marketing
Treating the entire market as one undifferentiated group
Niche marketing
Focusing on a narrow, specialised segment
Differentiated targeting
Serving several segments with separate mixes
Customer profile
A detailed description of the typical target customer
Positioning
The place a product occupies in the customer's mind versus rivals
Positioning map
A chart comparing brands on two key attributes
Repositioning
Changing how a product is perceived relative to competitors
Product Development and Branding: New product development
The process from idea generation through commercialisation
Idea screening
Eliminating concepts that do not fit company goals
Prototype
An early working model used to test a concept
Product life cycle
The stages of introduction, growth, maturity, and decline
Introduction stage
High costs, low sales, and heavy promotional spending
Growth stage
Rising sales, growing profits, and new competitors entering
Maturity stage
Peak sales with intense competition and price pressure
Decline stage
Falling sales requiring harvest or discontinuation decisions
Brand
A name, symbol, or design identifying a seller's product
Brand equity
The added value a strong brand name gives a product
Trademark
A brand element legally registered and protected
Private label brand
A product carrying the retailer's own brand name
Packaging functions
Protecting, informing, promoting, and enabling use of a product
Product differentiation
Making a product distinct from competing offerings
Pricing Strategies: Price
The amount of money exchanged for a product
Cost-plus pricing
Adding a fixed markup to the cost of producing an item
Markup
The amount added to cost to arrive at selling price
Break-even point
The sales level where total revenue equals total cost
Penetration pricing
Setting a low introductory price to gain market share quickly
Price skimming
Setting a high introductory price to maximise early profit
Competitive pricing
Setting prices in line with rival offerings
Psychological pricing
Using price points such as 9.99 to influence perception
Prestige pricing
Setting a high price to signal quality or status
Loss leader
A product priced below cost to draw customers into a store
Bundle pricing
Selling several products together for one combined price
Price elasticity of demand
How much quantity demanded responds to a price change
Discount and allowance
A reduction for volume, timing, or promotional cooperation
Distribution Channels: Distribution channel
The path a product takes from producer to final user
Direct channel
Selling from producer straight to the consumer
Indirect channel
Selling through one or more intermediaries
Wholesaler
An intermediary buying in bulk and reselling to retailers
Retailer
An intermediary selling directly to final consumers
Agent or broker
An intermediary arranging sales without taking ownership
Intensive distribution
Placing a product in as many outlets as possible
Selective distribution
Using a limited number of chosen outlets
Exclusive distribution
Granting one outlet sole rights in a territory
Supply chain
The full network from raw materials to the finished sale
Logistics
Planning and controlling the physical movement of goods
Inventory management
Balancing stock levels against holding cost and stockout risk
E-commerce channel
Selling through online platforms directly to buyers
Channel conflict
Disagreement among channel members over roles or pricing
Promotion and Advertising: Promotional mix
The blend of advertising, selling, sales promotion, and publicity
Advertising
Paid, nonpersonal communication through mass media
Publicity
Unpaid media coverage of a company or product
Public relations
Managing the organisation's image and relationships
Sales promotion
Short-term incentives such as coupons or contests
Personal selling
Direct one-to-one persuasion by a salesperson
Institutional advertising
Advertising that promotes the company image rather than a product
Promotional advertising
Advertising aimed at selling a specific product
Media planning
Choosing which channels will carry an advertising message
Reach and frequency
How many people see an ad versus how often they see it
Advertising appeal
The central persuasive angle, such as humour or fear
Call to action
The explicit instruction telling the audience what to do next
Truth in advertising laws
Regulations prohibiting false or deceptive claims
Digital and Social Media Marketing: Improving a site's ranking in unpaid search results
Paying only when a user clicks a placed ad
Attracting customers by publishing useful material
Building brand and sales through social platforms
Paying individuals with audiences to promote a product
The share of an audience interacting with content
The share of visitors completing a desired action
The share of viewers who click a link or ad
Sending targeted commercial messages to a subscriber list
Showing ads to users who previously visited a site
Measurement tools tracking digital campaign performance
Content spreading rapidly through voluntary sharing
Legal and ethical limits on collecting customer information
Selling and Customer Service: Personal selling process
Approach, presentation, objection handling, close, and follow-up
Prospecting
Identifying potential customers likely to buy
Qualifying a lead
Determining whether a prospect has need, authority, and means
Feature versus benefit
A product characteristic versus the advantage it gives the buyer
Objection
A customer concern raised during the sales process
Closing the sale
Securing the customer's agreement to buy
Trial close
A question testing whether the customer is ready to commit
Suggestion selling
Recommending additional items that complement the purchase
Follow-up
Contacting the customer after purchase to ensure satisfaction
Customer service
Activities that support customers before, during, and after a sale
Customer retention
Keeping existing customers rather than acquiring new ones
Handling complaints
Listening, apologising, resolving, and following through
Lifetime customer value
The total profit expected from a customer relationship
Marketing Plans: Marketing plan
A written document guiding marketing strategy and action
Executive summary
The brief opening overview of a marketing plan
Situation analysis
An assessment of current internal and external conditions
SWOT analysis
Evaluating strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats
Marketing objective
A specific, measurable goal the plan aims to achieve
SMART goal
A goal that is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and timed
Action plan
The scheduled tasks, owners, and deadlines for execution
Marketing budget
The money allocated to carry out the plan
Sales forecast
A projection of expected revenue over the plan period
Performance metric
A measure used to evaluate whether objectives are met
Return on investment
Profit generated relative to the cost of the campaign
Contingency plan
A prepared alternative if results miss expectations
Plan evaluation and control
Comparing results to objectives and adjusting the strategy
